name: Interior Painting Prep for Occupied Homes

mainEntity.name: What preparation should be included before interior painting in an occupied home?
mainEntity.text: What preparation should be included before interior painting in an occupied home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preparation is a major part of a quality interior paint job, especially when people are living in the home during the work. The contractor should cover furniture and floors, remove or mask fixtures, repair dents and nail holes, sand rough spots, caulk gaps, and prime stains or repaired areas as needed. In occupied homes, dust control and daily cleanup matter because sanding and prep can create a lot of debris. Ask how rooms will be staged, which spaces will be off limits, and how long paint fumes or drying times will affect use of the home. A detailed prep plan reduces delays, improves finish quality, and helps avoid damage to belongings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Interior painting in an occupied home should include protection of floors and furniture, patching, sanding, caulking, stain blocking, and dust control. Good preparation also means clear room-by-room scheduling so the home stays usable during the project. If prep is rushed, the finish usually shows defects and does not last as long.
